critiques.issue: E113 shows that a math-neutral fp change fully decorrelates every seed's trajectory (paired-difference sd 0.36 pp = sqrt(2) x 0.26). So a different cuDNN pick set in a new process is just another draw from the same per-trajectory distribution (sd ~0.26 pp). That one-component model already explains everything H4 splits into three parts. The scored 3-seed run-to-run sd should be 0.26/sqrt(3) ≈ 0.15 pp, and the observed E101 0.7561 vs 0.7516 is ~2 SD of the difference, so it is plausible. The 22-seed process sd should be ~0.055 pp. The supposed 'disagreement' with E106's 0.03 pp comes from an sd estimated from n=3 processes, which has a 90% CI of roughly 0.25x–2.2x. H4.5 (clustered per-process offsets) and H4.7 (side script differs from the harness) are explaining sampling noise in an sd estimate.
critiques.suggestion: Rewrite H4 as a single-component model: per-trajectory sd ~0.26 pp, and processes are independent unless their runs are bit-identical. Retire H4.5 and H4.7, or demote both to free log analysis with no new runs. Recompute the expected sd of every instrument from 0.26/sqrt(n_distinct_trajectories).

critiques.issue: H4.6 says more processes do not reduce recipe re-draw noise and only more seeds do. E113 contradicts this. Seed pairing gives zero variance reduction, so a seed carries no persistent component, and a non-bit-identical process on the same seeds is as informative as new seeds. The 'recipe re-draw' and 'process' components are the same thing.
critiques.suggestion: Correct H4.6. Effective n = the number of distinct (non-bit-identical) trajectories, whether they come from new seeds or new processes. Drop the claim that pairing helps, and stop calling the large-seed A/Bs 'paired'. They are two-sample comparisons with SE = 0.26*sqrt(1/nA + 1/nB).

critiques.issue: E113 already answers the persistent seeds-0-2 offset hypothesis. If the same seed under a neutral perturbation has zero correlation with itself, seeds 0-2 cannot carry a recipe-specific persistent offset. E100's five distinct scored samples (mean 0.7543, SE ~0.15/sqrt(5) ≈ 0.067) sit ~0.15 SE from its 100-seed mean (0.7530–0.7533). That is no evidence of an offset.
critiques.suggestion: Retire H4.8 without running H4.8.1. State in H4 that gate passes are population margin plus luck. At a population mean of ~0.753, the per-run pass probability is ~50–60%.

structured_output.summary:
The most important correction is to the noise model. E113 shows that any fp-level perturbation fully decorrelates each seed's trajectory, so the noise reduces to one component: per-trajectory sd ~0.26 pp, with seed pairing giving no benefit. Under that model, H4's three components, H4.5 (cuDNN clustering), H4.7 (side-script mismatch) and H4.8 (a persistent seeds-0-2 offset) are explaining sampling noise and should be retired. The "disagreement" between E101 and E106 comes from an sd estimated from n=3 processes.

The model also inflates past SEs. Most 8–22-seed off-seed verdicts are about 1 SE: E084, E104, E092, E079 and E078. Only E093 and E083 are clearly real. So H10's update-count rate and its "update count, not path length" mechanism are unsupported, as are the averaging magnitudes that H9.2 relies on and the 0.065 pp per 1% trim rate used to judge every lever.

E114 nulled the H8.2-vs-H11 reallocation question. H8 and H11 add little now, and H9's structural/scalar split was drawn after the results came in.

The surprising result is E116. A late freeze of the stem and group 1 saved 3.6–4.5% of time with a real but small loss: about −0.09 pp against a pooled 200-trajectory baseline, or ~0.025 pp per 1%, the best recent trade. The saving is well above group 1's FLOP share, which points to backward activation bytes at 31x31 in an energy-bound phase. No current hypothesis predicted this. It also reopens group-1 width and stem stride, which were never tested under Muon.

Next steps:
- Pool E113's two E100 arms as the baseline.
- Re-measure the trim rate on 100+ seeds.
- Run a dose-response on the freeze point.
- Write an explicit decision rule for the gap between the official 0.75 bar, where there is ~0.3 pp of slack, and the noisy local 0.753 gate. That choice decides whether E116-class levers can be banked.

Also fix the evidence tokens whose signs contradict their nodes' status.
